spans.s:
√lup (lumpáti [758]; lulópa; luptá;
lóptum; luptvā́; -lúpya).
 —1. break;
harm;
 —2. attack; pounce upon;
 —3.
rob, plunder. [younger form of √rup:
cf. Lat. rumpere, ‘break’; AS. reōf-an,
‘break’; reāf, ‘spoil of battle, booty,
armor, etc., esp. clothing, garments,’ Ger.
Raub, ‘robbery, booty’; AS. reāfian,
‘despoil, rob,’ whence Eng. reave, ppl.
reft, and be-reave: fr. Old High Ger.
roubōn, ‘rob,’ through Old French rober,
‘rob,’ comes French dé-rober, Eng. rob,
and fr. Old High Ger. roub, ‘robbery,
booty, esp. pillaged garment,’ in like
manner, French robe, ‘garment,’ Eng.
robe.]
